sentences.text: Similicaudipteryx is a genus of theropod dinosaur belonging to the family Caudipteridae.
Like its relative Caudipteryx, this animal had a short snout with a lower jaw curved downward, along with relatively short arms and long legs.
It possessed a unique dagger-shaped pygostyle made of the two most extreme tail vertebrae, a feature not found in its relatives.
Similicaudipteryx also had an exceptionally long pubic bone relative to the ilium.
Researchers speculate feathers were present because the pygostyle serves as an anchor point for tail feathers in modern birds.
Gregory S. Paul estimated the length of Similicaudipteryx at one meter and its weight at seven kilograms in 2010.
The genus Similicaudipteryx was named and described in 2008 by He Tao, Wang Xiaolin, and Zhou Zonghe.
The holotype consists of a nearly complete adult skeleton that lacks the skull, front neck, and hands.
In 2010, two additional juvenile specimens with feather preservation were referred to Similicaudipteryx, but have since been re-interpreted as belonging to Incisivosaurus gauthieri.
Although the holotype lacks feather traces, researchers speculate feathers were present because the pygostyle serves as an anchor point for tail feathers in modern birds.

The describers assigned Similicaudipteryx to the family Caudipteridae without performing an exact cladistic analysis of its position, though a later analysis by Lamanna et al. placed it within the same family.
Similicaudipteryx lived during the middle Cretaceous Period, approximately 124 to 120 million years ago, in what is now Asia, with a time range estimated between 121.4 and 113.2 million years ago.
In 2010, Gregory S. Paul renamed the species Caudipteryx yixianensis, but this change has not been accepted by the scientific community.
